name: Winter arc lock-in
tagline: Five things to lock in before the cold gets to your hair.
image_alt: Chunky two-strand twists parted off the hairline, resting over one shoulder.
description: Five winter hair-care moves: a calm scalp routine, a gentler cleanser, ceramides, warm conditioner, and getting your vitamin D, iron and ferritin checked.
intro: Cold air outside, dry heat inside, hats and scarves rubbing your hair all day. Winter is a lot. This plan is five simple locks to go all in on this season, one at a time.

causes.title: Why winter is hard on hair
causes.intro: None of this is your fault. It's just the season.
items: Dry air, inside and out
Cold air holds less moisture, and indoor heating dries it out even more.
Hair and scalp can feel drier and tighter than usual.
Hats, scarves and collars
Fabric rubbing against your hair all day.
Friction roughens the surface of the strand and tangles ends. Satin or silk lining makes a difference.
Long, hot showers
Hot water feels amazing when it's freezing out.
It can leave scalp and hair drier. Lukewarm for hair is kinder.
Less of everything else
Less sleep, more stress, a heavier schedule.
Your body and your hair feel it too, which is why the last lock is a check-up.

routine.title: The five locks
routine.intro: You don't have to do all five on day one. Start with the one that feels easiest and add the next.

washes.title: Lock it in
steps: Add a leave-on scalp serum with green tea extract (EGCG), like The Ordinary's, to a calm, consistent scalp routine. Green tea may help slow winter shedding and keep your scalp comfortable. Part your hair, apply a little to the scalp, and massage gently with your fingertips.

steps.note: The research on green tea is early, so think of it as support, not a cure. If you notice a lot more shedding than usual, or patchy thinning, see a doctor or dermatologist first.
link: Read about green tea, caffeine, niacinamide and the other scalp actives
steps.label: A simple serum to start with

steps: Cold air and dry heat already pull moisture out of your hair, and a strong shampoo adds to that. For your regular winter washes, look for a level 1 cleanser, one built on mild cleansers like isethionates, taurates or glucosides. Save stronger ones for an occasional reset. Remember that "sulfate-free" doesn't always mean gentle, so check which cleanser comes first on the label.

steps.note: If your hair feels coated and your products stop working, a stronger clarifying wash now and then is fine. Just follow it with a deep conditioner.
link: See the cleanser levels, from 1 (gentlest) to 4 (strongest)
steps.label: A level 1 shampoo to try

steps: Use a conditioner, mask or leave-in with ceramides to support the lipids on the surface of your hair. Winter is a great time to do this weekly. It works alongside your regular conditioner, it doesn't replace it.

Cold conditioner is stiff and hard to spread. Stand the bottle or tub in a bowl of warm (not hot) water for a few minutes first, or use a heat cap. It will spread more easily and feel like a treat. Never microwave a bottle.

Ask your doctor about checking your vitamin D, iron and ferritin. These are some of the things doctors look at when someone is concerned about shedding or tired hair. Please get tested before you supplement. Too much iron can be harmful, and only a test tells you what you actually need.

steps.note: We can't tell you what's going on in your body from your hair, and a product can't replace a blood test. This is a conversation to have with your doctor.

between.title: Every day this winter
groups: Check your ends. If they feel dry, add a little leave-in.
Wear a satin-lined hat or put a scarf over a satin cap.
Loose styles. Nothing tight on cold, dry hair.

trouble.title: If something feels off
items: Scalp itchy or flaky
Dry winter air is a common cause, but flaking and itching can have other causes too. If it doesn't settle, ask a doctor or dermatologist.
Hair feels stiff and dry
Go back to a moisturising conditioner and warm it up. Check for buildup before you add anything.
More shedding than usual
See your doctor. Bring up vitamin D, iron and ferritin, and anything else going on with your health, medicines or stress.
Tangles at the ends
Look at friction first: hats, scarves, collars. Satin lining helps.

end.title: By the end of winter
notes: Winter is a season, and your hair will bounce back. Keep whichever locks you liked, drop the ones you didn't, and keep your photos from December to compare.
